reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly: order 122 for 5470 and order 124 for 1085. Next I'll list the orders to confirm the refunded orders exist and that the batch is consistent before computing payouts.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly, and both refunded orders exist with amounts above their refunds. Nothing looks wrong, so I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance came back as 31368. Next I'll get birch's net balance, since birch has refund 124 applied.

Acme (31368) and birch (19998) both match order totals minus refunds, so Alpha's refunds look consistent so far. Cobalt is the last customer with a refund, order 122, so I'll check its net balance next.

All three net balances match order totals minus refunds: acme 31368, birch 19998, cobalt 24286. The ledger refunds match Alpha's handoff, so there's no concrete problem to hold for. I'll record acme's payout first.

Acme's payout recorded successfully. I checked birch and cobalt against the order totals and refunds: birch is 8002 + 13081 - 1085 = 19998 and cobalt is 7562 + 22194 - 5470 = 24286, both matching. Nothing is wrong, so I'll record birch's payout.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's net balance of 24286 matches 7562 + 22194 - 5470, so I'll record its payout now.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each matches its customer's order total minus refunds, and the ledger refunds matched Alpha's handoff, so the batch is complete.
